title: Validity: Face, Content, Criterion, Construct
summary: Concept of validity; types (face, content, criterion - concurrent/predictive, construct); convergent and discriminant validity; relationship between reliability and validity.
revision: Validity = measures what it claims. Types: face, content, criterion (concurrent/predictive), construct (convergent/discriminant). Reliable ≠ valid; valid → usually reliable.
traps: Valid test must be reliable; reliable test need not be valid.

notes.t: The extent to which a test measures what it claims to measure.

r: Test appears to measure what it claims
A math test with math questions
Test correlates with an external criterion

i: Concurrent validity: test and criterion measured at the same time.
Predictive validity: test predicts future criterion performance.
Convergent validity: correlates with measures of the same construct.
Discriminant validity: does not correlate with measures of different constructs.

r: Does it measure what it claims?
A test can be reliable but not valid
A valid test is usually reliable

notes.t: A test can be reliable without being valid, but a valid test must be reliable. This distinction is frequently tested in UGC NET.
